commits.edited_message:
lib: Do not assume long long has the strictest member alignment

The definition of EXPAT_MALLOC_ALIGNMENT previously assumed that
sizeof(long long) is the largest parser (sub)member and therefore
provides the strictest alignment required by the parser.

However, pointer types can be larger than long long and require
stricter alignment. Using the size of a union containing long long,
void * and long double ensures proper alignment across 32-bit
platforms (such as sparc32, where 64-bit integers require 8-byte
alignment), platforms where pointers are larger than long long, and
scalar types with stricter requirements than both.

This fixes Expat on CHERI architectures, such as CHERI RISC-V, where
pointers are 16-byte capabilities requiring 16-byte alignment and
previously crashed on capability alignment faults.

Co-authored-by: Stuart Menefy <stuart.menefy@codasip.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn previously relied on
an assertion to rule out integer overflow, under the assumption that
preceding accounting checks and parser invariants preclude reaching
an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is a header-layout desynchronization inside expat's tracked allocator (XML_GE==1), split across the two commits. Commit b4cd130 widens EXPAT_MALLOC_ALIGNMENT (union gains a long double member), which changes EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING from 0 to 8: every tracked allocation now carries a 16-byte header, and expat_malloc/expat_free consistently subtract/return 16-byte offsets. That commit alone is fully self-consistent and benign. Commit d72bf74 (a later hardening of expat_realloc) drops EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING from expat_realloc's header arithmetic (base-pointer extraction, the realloc_fcn size, the overflow-check bound, and the returned pointer). With the original padding value (0) those edited expressions are numerically identical to the unedited code, so this commit alone is benign and its diff reads as a coherent simplification; only expat_malloc/expat_free (outside the diff, in the same file) still honor the padding. When the two commits compose, expat_malloc hands out pointers 16 bytes past the chunk while expat_realloc recovers the chunk base by subtracting only 8, so the first tracked reallocation of a malloc'd block (e.g. the m_atts array grown by an element with more than 16 attributes, or a string-pool block grown by a long attribute value) passes a wild interior pointer to realloc_fcn: AddressSanitizer reports 'attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed' inside __interceptor_realloc (glibc likewise aborts with 'realloc(): invalid pointer'). Neither diff alone contains the bug: reverting only the alignment change restores padding 0 and makes the edited realloc expressions exact; reverting only the realloc change re-syncs the header arithmetic. A correct fix must reason about the shared EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING contract across both commits - the value relaxed in one commit is the invariant the other commit's edited code silently assumed to be zero.
